entries.reason: HIBP k-anonymity requires a SHA-1 lookup prefix; the digest is never used for authentication, signatures, or password storage and hashlib is explicitly called with usedforsecurity=False.
The insecure origin is a loopback-only Vite HMR development endpoint; production configuration never reaches this branch and maps HTTPS application origins to secure WebSocket transport.
This is not a Flask route: it returns an internal rate-limit key containing only a SHA-256 digest of an HttpOnly cookie, never attacker-controlled HTML or a response body.

PostgreSQL publication names are identifiers and cannot be bound as asyncpg parameters; the value is reduced to alphanumeric characters/underscore before interpolation, with the source name fixed by trusted configuration and covered by provisioning tests.
This call uses an asyncpg replication connection rather than SQLAlchemy; the only interpolated token is the sanitized publication identifier, while all data-bearing queries use positional parameters.

The build-time VITE_BACKEND_ORIGIN is escaped character-by-character before interpolation into a fixed /api/ prefix; it is not request data and regression tests cover metacharacter escaping and same-origin fallback.

Markdown and legacy article content are sanitized/HTML-escaped by sanitizeArticleHtml before rendering; the component has no raw HTML path and sanitizer regression tests cover script and event-handler payloads.

The value is produced by the allowlist-based WASM/ammonia sanitizer and then checked for script and event-handler patterns; unsafe output falls back to plain text and dedicated tests cover bypass attempts.

SPIRE's Kubernetes workload attestor must resolve node/container PIDs; hostPID is an intentional documented trust boundary, while the pod is non-privileged, drops capabilities, and uses RuntimeDefault seccomp.

SPIRE's node-local agent socket and workload attestor require host networking; this is the documented agent trust boundary, restricted by service-account RBAC, non-privileged containers, and pinned images.

The load-test target is explicit operator input, restricted to http/https with no embedded credentials and a required hostname before urlopen; chaos tooling is not an application request path, and tests cover rejected schemes. HTTP fragments are not transmitted by the client.
The URL is constructed from the fixed api.github.com origin and a fullmatched Actions endpoint; tests cover rejection of every other endpoint and HTTPS is required.
The host, port, redirect policy, and bounded request target are validated before an explicit system-trust TLS context is passed to HTTPSConnection; transport tests cover the boundary.
The URL uses the fixed api.github.com origin and a strict current-run path allowlist; the request uses an explicit verified TLS context and bounded response reader.

The package-level gorilla Upgrader uses CheckOrigin=isUpgradeOriginAllowed; explicit WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS allowlists reject unknown non-empty origins before ticket consumption/upgrade, while empty Origin is intentionally accepted only for native clients. handlers_edge_cases_test.go and handlers_unit_test.go cover allowed and rejected origins.
